NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Part 3) which is identical with IS0 8630-3 : 1987 `Information processingData interchange on 130 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges using modified frequency modulation recording at 13 262 ftprad on 80 tracks on each side - Part 3 : Track format B for 80 tracks' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 December 1989 on the recommendation of the Computers, Business Machines and Calculators Sectional Committee (LTD 24) and approval of Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. In the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical with those used in Indian Standards, attention is specially drawn to the following : a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) Comma (,) has been used as a decimal markgr while in Indian Standards the current practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker. c) For the purpose of Indian Standard, metric dimensions shall be applicable. Introduction

3

References
IS0 7-bit coded character

IS0 8630 specifies the characteristics of 136 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges recorded at 13 262 ftprad, using modified frequency modulation (MFM) recording, on 80 tracks on each side. IS0 8630-l specifies the dimensional, physical and magnetic characteristics of the cartridge, so as to provide physical interchangeability between data processing systems. IS0 8530-2 specifies an alternative track format for data interchange. IS0 963&l and IS0 8630-3, together with the labelling scheme specified in IS0 9293, provide for full data interchange between data processing systems.

IS0 646, Information processing set for information interchange.

IS0 2022, information proces&ng - IS0 Fbit and 8-bit coded character sets - Code extension techniques. IS0 4973, Information processing - IS0 8-bit code for information interchange - Structure and rules for implementation. IS0 6429, information processing 7 IS0 7-bit and 8-bit character sets - Additional control functions for characterimaging devices. IS0 9293, Information processing - Volume and file structure of flexible disk cartridges for information interchange.

4 1 Scope and field of application
4.1

General requirements
Mode of recording

This part of IS0 6636 specifies the qualhy of recorded signals, the track layout, and a track format to be used on 135 mm (5.25 in), 13 262 ftprad flexible disk cartridges intended for data interchange between data processing systems. NOTE - Numeric values in the SI and/or Imperial measurament~ system in this part of IS0 8630 may have been rounded off and therefore are consistentwith, but not exactly equal to, each other. Either systemmay be used, but the two shouldbe neither intermixed nor re-converted.The originaldesignwes made using Imperial units and further developments were made usingSI units.

The mode of recording shall be Modified Frequency Modulation (MFM) for which the conditions are a) a flux transition shall be written at the centre of each bit cell containing a ONE; b) a flux transition shall be written at each cw dundary between consecutive bit cells containing ZEROS. Exceptions to this are defined in 4.12.

4.5

Average Signal Amplitude

At the instant of writing or reading a magnetic transition, the transition shall have an angle of O" It 18' with the radius. NOTE - As tracks may be written and overwrittenat extremesof the tolerances givenin 4.2 and 4.3, a band of old information may be left at one edge of the newly written date and would constitute unwanted
noise when reading. It is therefore necessary to trim the edges of the tracks by erasure after writing.

For each side the Average Signal Amplitude on any track (see IS0 8830-l J of the interchanged flexible disk cartridge shall be less than 180 % of SRA,,and more than 40 % of MAW

4.7

Byte

A byte is a group of eight bit-positions, identified 81 to B8. The bit in each position is a ZERO or a ONE. 4.8 Sector

4.4

Density of recording
All tracks shall he divided into 15 sectors of 512 bytes. 4.9 Cylinder

4.4.1 The nominal density of recording shall be 13 282 ftprad". The resulting nominal bit cell length is 75.5 urad. 4.4.2 The long-term average bit cell length shall be the average bit cell length measured over a sector. It shall be within f 3,0 % of the nominal bit cell length. 4.4.3 The short-term average bit cell length, referred to a particular bit cell, shall be the average of the lengths of the preceding eight bit cells. It shall be within f 8 96 of the longterm average bit cell length. 4.5

A pair of tracks, one on each side of the disk, having the same track number.

4.10

Cylinder Number

The Cylinder Number shall be a two-digit number identical with the track number of the tracks of the cylinder. 4.11

Flux tran'sition spacing (see figure 1)

Data capacity of a track

The instantaneous spacing between flux transitions may be influenced by the reading and writing process, the bit sequence recorded (pulse crowding effects) and other factors. The locations of the transitions are defined as the locations of the peaks in the signal when reading. Tests should be carried out using a peak-sensing read amplifier (see annexes B and C). 4.5.1 The spacing between the flux transitions in a sequence of ONES shall be between 80 % and 120 % of the short-term average bit cell length. 4.5.2 The spacing betwaen the flux transition for a ONE and that between two ZEROs preceding or following it shall be between 130 % and 185 % of the short-term average bii cell length. 4.5.3 The spacing between the flux transitions of two ONEs surrounding a ZERO shall lie between 185 % and 225 % of the short-term average bit cell length.

The data capacity of a track shall be 7 880 bytes.

5.1

Index Gap

This field shall specify in binary notation the Cylinder Number from 99 for the outermost cylinder to 79 for the innermost cylinder. b) Side Number (Side)

At nominal density, this field shall comprise not less than 92 bytes and not more than 146 bytes, the content of which is not specified except that it shall not contain an (Al)*-byte. Writing' the Index Gap is started when the index hole is detected. Any of the first 16 bytes may become ill-defined due to subsequent overwriting.

This field shall specify the side of the disk. On side 0 it shall be (00) on all tracks. On side 1 it shall be (01) on all tracks. 5.2.2.2 Sector Number W

5.2

The contents of the Data Field shall be recorded and interpreted according to the relevant International Standards for the coding of information, for example IS0 646, IS0 2622 or IS0 4873. 6.2 Coding methods

6.2.1 When the coding method requires it, the Data Field shall be regarded as an ordered sequence of 6-bit bytes. Within each byte the bit positions shall be identified by B8 to Bl. The high-order bit shall be recorded in position 88 and the low-order bit in position Bl. The sequence of recording shall be high-order bit first. When the data is encoded according to an 8-bit code, the binary weights of the bit positions shall be as shown in figure 3.

These two bytes shall be generated as defined in 4.13 using the bytes of the Data Block starting with the first (Al )*-byte of the . Annex A EDC implementation
(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

Figure 4 shows the feedback connections of a shift register which may be used to generate the EDC bvtes. Prior to operation, all positions of the shift register are set to ONE. Input data are added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position Cta of the register to form a feedback. This feedback is in its turn added (exclusive OR) to the contents of position C,Jand position Ctt. On shifting, the outputs of the exclusive OR gates are entered respectively into positions Cc, C5 and C12. After the last data bit has been added, the register is shifted once more as specified above. The register then contains the EUC bytes. If further shifting is to take place during the writing of the FDC bytes, the control signal inhibits exclusive OR operations. To check for errors when reading, the data bits are added into the shift register in exactly the same manner as they were during writing. After the data, the EDC bytes are also entered into the shift register as if they were data. After the final shift, the register contents will be all ZERO if the record `does not contain errors.

(for EDC writing)

Annex Procedure and equipment

B flux transition spacing

for measuring

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

B.l

General

This annex specifies equipment and a procedure for measuring flux transition spacing on 130 mm (5.25 in) flexible disk cartridges using MFM recording at 13 262 ftprad on both sides.

8.2

Format

The disk to be measured shall be written by the disk drive for data interchange use. Testing shall be done on tracks 00 and 76 on both sides. On all test tracks the test patterns 11011011 (LIB) and 11011100 (DC) shall be written repeatedly.

8.3
6.3.1

Test equipment
Disk drive

The disk drive shall have a rotational speed of 360 r/min, with a tolerance of + 3 rlmin, averaged over one revolution. The average angular speed, taken over 32 ms, shall not deviate by more than 0,5 96 from the speed averaged over one revolution. 0.3.2 8.3.2.1 Head Resolution

The head shall have an absolute resolution of 55 % to 65 % at track 76 on side 0 and at track 66 on side 1, using the reference material RM 6630, applying the calibration'factor of the reference material, and recording with the appropriate test recording current. The resonant frequency of the head shall be at least 500 006 Hz. The resolution shall not be adjusted by varying the load impedance of the head. The resolution shall be measured at the output of the amplifier defined in 6.3.3.1. 6.3.2.2 Offset angle

The head shall have a gap offset angle of do t 6' with the disk radius on the testing drive. 0.3.2.3 Contact

Care shall be taken that the heads are in good contact with the media during the tests.

6.3.3 8.3.3.1

Read

channel

Read amplifier

The read amplifier shall have a flat response from 1 000 to 375 000 Hz within zt 1 dB, and amplitude saturation shall not occur. 8.3.3.2 Peak sensing amplifier

Peak sensing shall be carried out by a differentiating and limiting amplifier.

8

IS 12327 [Part 3) : 1989 IS0 8630-3 : 1987

8.3.4

Time interval measuring equipment

The time interval counter shall be able to measure 2 us to at least 5 ns resolution. A triggering oscilloscope may be used for this purpose.

8.4
8.4.1

Procedure for measurement
Flux transition spacing measurement

The transition locations shall be measured by the locations of the peaks in the signal when reading. The flux transition spacing shall be measured by the pulse timing intervals after the read channel amplifier defined in 53.3. 6.4.2

spacing

for all tracks

Annex Data separators

C MFM recording

for decoding

(This annex does not form part of the standard.)

C.l

On track 00, side 0 the two-frequency recording results in nominal flux transition periods of

t for a ONE cell
2t where for a ZERO cell

t = 2 us.

The data separator shall be capable of resolving a difference of 2 us. This can be achieved satisfactorily by the use of a digital data separator, or one using a fixed timer.

C.2

On all other tracks the MFM recording method gives nominal flux transition spacings of

t for the patterns 11 or OW
3tf2 for the patterns 10 or 01

21 for the pattern 101 The data separator should be capable of resolving a difference of 1 us. To achieve this with'a low error rate, the separator cannot operate on a fixed period but should follow changes in the bit cell length. It is recognized that various techniques may be developed to achieve dynamic data separation; with present technology only an analogue data separator based on a phase-locked oscillator can provide the necessary reliability.
